title: First Thing: Trump welcomes Xi to Washington amid tensions over trade, AI and Taiwan
summary:
State visit takes place at same time as UN general assembly, which Chinese leader has avoided. Plus, meet the people who are real-life Pokémon ‘professors’

Good morning.

blocks.text: Good morning. Donald Trump has welcomed Xi Jinping to the US, greeting the Chinese leader on the tarmac at Joint Base Andrews at the start of his state visit. Xi’s trip coincides with the UN general assembly in New York, but he is not attending the gathering.

The pageantry will continue with a formal welcome on the South Lawn of the White House, private tea with the US president and first lady, and a tour of the National Archives, among other special events. The White House has also invited major tech leaders to a state dinner being held for Xi.

items: What will the two leaders discuss? Amy Hawkins note in this explainer that topics are likely to include the development of AI technology, frosty trade relations and Taiwan.

What developments have there been in US-China relations? The US treasury secretary, Scott ⁠Bessent, announced that the US ⁠and ​China agreed on Wednesday to extend the so-called Busan ⁠agreement – a temporary trade truce between the world’s two biggest economies.

Who else has been invited to the US? The US has invited Vladimir Putin to take part in the G20 meeting scheduled to take place in Miami in December, in what would be the Russian leader’s first attendance at such a summit since he launched his invasion of Ukraine in 2022. The US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, said: “We hope that’s an invitation he’ll accept.”

blocks.text: Iran’s president hits out at ‘bully’ Trump in UN speech

blocks.caption: Iran’s president, Masoud Pezeshkian. Photograph: Timothy A Clary/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: In a defiant speech to the UN general assembly in New York, Iran’s president, Masoud Pezeshkian described the US as the true bully and terrorist in the Middle East while insisting that Iran had always shown a commitment to the negotiating table. But he balanced that with a willingness to talk, saying: “We are ready for dialogue and diplomacy and negotiations but without the language of force.”

Pezeshkian accused Washington of “terrorism” for assassinating the country’s supreme leader, Ali Khamenei, at the start of the US-Israeli war. He held up photographs of the ayatollah and some of the more than 150 schoolchildren killed in the opening days of the conflict. He also insisted that Tehran had never started a war.

items: Why is Israel facing a water supply crisis? Israel is facing weeks of water shortages after an exceptional algae bloom crippled much of its desalination capacity, in a crisis scientists say was triggered when Israeli attacks destroyed much of Gaza’s wastewater infrastructure, causing a huge discharge of untreated sewage.

blocks.text: Judge orders White House to restore access to CNN, MS Now and Politico

blocks.caption: Donald Trump gives a press conference in the Oval Office. Photograph: Bloomberg/Getty Images

blocks.text: In a blow for the administration and Donald Trump’s repeated attacks on US media outlets, a federal judge has ordered the White House to temporarily restore ⁠access ​to journalists from CNN, MS Now and Politico. The US district judge Tim Kelly said the ban on the three media outlets was ⁠likely to be unconstitutional.

A lawyer for the Department of Justice told Kelly the administration had provided a enough explanation for the revocation of the ​press passes, but the judge signalled skepticism of that argument, ​noting that the letters were sent after the revocation occurred and the lawsuit was filed.

items: Where else has Trump suffered a legal setback over media coverage? A judge has also dismissed Trump’s lawsuit accusing the Des Moines Register and its former pollster of misrepresenting the state of the 2024 presidential race, rejecting the president’s claim that the newspaper’s poll coverage violated Iowa’s consumer fraud law.

blocks.text: Eight USS Lincoln personnel have attempted suicide, US navy confirms

blocks.caption: The USS Abraham Lincoln. Photograph: Chanakarn Laosarakham/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Eight US navy personnel assigned to the USS Abraham Lincoln carrier strike group have attempted to take their own lives since the start of their lengthy deployment as part of the US war on Iran, the acting US navy secretary, Hung Cao, revealed in a letter to Senator Kirsten Gillibrand. Donald Trump described reports of poor conditions on the ship as fake news in August.

In the US, you can call or text the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline at 988 or chat at 988lifeline.org. In the UK and Ireland, Samaritans can be contacted on freephone 116 123. In Australia, the crisis support service Lifeline is 13 11 14. Other international helplines can be found at befrienders.org
In other news …

blocks.caption: The US senator Susan Collins. Photograph: Jonathan Ernst/Reuters

items: Democrats accused the Republican senator Susan Collins of corruption after a major media outlet reported that the FBI had proposed investigating her for allegedly accepting bribes. Collins has disputed the report.
The FBI is investigating an apparent breach of its jobs website after a criminal hacking group claimed to have accessed “very sensitive data” on nearly all agents and job applicants.
Harvey Weinstein was sentenced to 15 years after being convicted of sexually assaulting the former TV production assistant Miriam Haley in 2006 at his Manhattan apartment.
The Former NFL star Antonio Brown plans to accept a plea deal on an attempted murder charge. Doing so will mean the former wide receiver avoids prison.
Meta announced a new set of virtual reality glasses and a collection of new smart glasses, including an audio-only version without a camera.

blocks.text: Stat of the day: RFK Jr received $4m in book advances from Maha allies over past year

blocks.caption: Robert F Kennedy Jr. Photograph: Jacquelyn Martin/AP

blocks.text: The US health secretary, Robert F Kennedy Jr, received $4m in book advances over the last year from allies in the Make America Healthy Again movement. According to a 2024 ethics filing, however, he pledged: “I will not engage in writing, editing, marketing or promotional services for any of these books during government service.” A spokesperon for the Department of Health and Human Services said Kennedy Jr “complies with all applicable federal ethics laws, regulations and financial disclosure requirements”.

… or this: ‘I miss old Google’ – readers tell us how they search the internet in the age of AI

blocks.caption: Google’s AI mode. Photograph: Matteo Della Torre/NurPhoto/Getty Images

blocks.text: I am old enough to remember the 1990s when internet search was mostly haphazard guesswork, then Google came along and you could actually find things. Now you can’t again. Google’s insertion of AI overviews has profoundly changed the browsing habits of billions of people. Guardian readers explain their new search strategies.

blocks.text: Oliver Milman reports on how the former US vice-president is still optimistic about climate advocacy two decades after the groundbreaking documentary.
Last Thing: In historic first, tropical turtles spotted nesting on California beaches

blocks.caption: An olive ridley turtle hatchling. Photograph: Aman Rochman/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock

blocks.text: “This is the first documented case of a turtle nesting on the west coast,” Justin Viezbicke, the California stranding coordinator for the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Association (Noaa) said. What caused the turtles to begin nesting farther north than usual remains an open question.
